$comment: Generated by scripts/generate-yjs-engine-fixtures.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
$description: HAND-ASSEMBLED malformed updates (the v2 case excepted; it says so). Every case must be REFUSED by the C# decoder. `yjsAccepts` records what real yjs does with the same bytes — where it is true, yjs is the lenient one and the engine is deliberately stricter.

cases.name: truncated-varstring
cases.description: The parentSub varstring announces five bytes and only one follows.

cases.name: varuint-over-2pow53
cases.description: The leading struct-group count is a varuint whose value passes 2^53.

cases.name: invalid-utf8-key
cases.description: The root name is a two-byte varstring holding a lead byte with no continuation byte.

cases.name: trailing-garbage-after-delete-set
cases.description: A valid update with one extra byte after the delete set; a v1 reader never checks for it.

cases.name: client-listed-twice
cases.description: Two struct groups name client 1000; yjs Map.set silently keeps the last one.

cases.name: unknown-content-ref-11
cases.description: The info byte names content ref 11; only 0-10 exist and 0/10 are not item content.

cases.name: parentsub-bit-without-parent
cases.description: The info byte sets the parentSub bit and neither origin bit, then the buffer ends before the parent info.

cases.name: v2-update
cases.description: A real Y.encodeStateAsUpdateV2 payload. Its leading 00 reads as zero struct groups, so a v1 reader swallows it whole and returns an empty update.
cases.note: The only case here produced by yjs rather than assembled by hand.
